properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony thinking out loud, 2026-08-11. Nothing here is intent.

HIS FRAMING, in his words: "feedback that I've been giving back to from various projects... is clear demand signal of what needs prioritized... Obviously, this is demand signal for reflow2 itself; perhaps, in a general project, this would be akin to 'test reports', which should help prioritize which things need fixed immediately versus other desirements." And the sharpening that prompted it: two items in a fresh external report were things ALREADY ACCEPTED and unbuilt, so the report did not propose them — it CONFIRMED them, which is a different and more actionable signal.

THE MEASUREMENT, taken 2026-08-11 on this design:

  TemporalFact nodes                                    133
    of fact_type `defect`                               123   — every one basis: measured
    of those, whose text describes RECURRENCE            70   (instance / recurred / third time /
                                                               two projects / again)
  ranking computations that read any of them              0

`what_next` scores connectedness only: governed nodes (+1 each), those scheduled into an increment (+2), CONTRADICTS an accepted Decision (+2). `crates/reflow2-core/src/what_next.rs` never references TEMPORAL_FACT. The only readers anywhere are nodes.rs (constants), temporal.rs (the writer), preserve.rs (classification) and readiness.rs (forecasts). So reflow2 holds a corpus of 123 measured field observations and cannot let one of them move a priority.

⭐ THE WORKED EXAMPLE IS FROM TODAY AND IT COST FORTY MINUTES. `fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server` (2026-08-07) recorded a defect at basis `measured`, confidence 1, WITH ITS FIX WRITTEN IN ITS OWN EVIDENCE FIELD. A sibling fact counted three instances across two projects and two machines and noted the third "landed on the maintainer". A fourth instance hit on 2026-08-11 and blocked every graph tool. Between the diagnosis and the fix, FOUR DAYS, during which nothing ranked it — because a TemporalFact is not a Decision and `what_next` scores Decisions. The issue it was filed under was CLOSED with the finding unfixed.

⚠️⚠️ THE DECISIVE COUNTER-ARGUMENT IS ANTHONY'S OWN, AND IT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED. `dec:proposed-requirements-pruned` (2026-07-30) DROPPED `req:friction-has-a-severity-bar` and `req:friction-has-a-baseline` with this reason: "Both are backlog hygiene dressed as product requirements: THE ANSWER TO UNCONVERTED FRICTION REPORTS IS TO ACT ON THEM, NOT TO MODEL THEM." His stated test was whether a requirement changes what anyone BUILDS, and "how the project manages itself" does not. Any version of this idea has to answer that or it is a re-litigation.

THE ARGUMENT THAT IT IS NOT THE SAME THING, offered so he can judge it rather than be persuaded by it: the dropped pair were about REFLOW2 MEASURING ITSELF — a usability baseline, and a threshold at which reflow2's own friction becomes reflow2's own scheduled work. That is process. THIS is about whether ANY user's design can let measured field evidence — test reports, incident records, trial findings — reach the thing that says what to work on next. That is a product capability with a code citation, which is exactly what survived his prune. The honest counter to the counter: it is also convenient for me to say so, and he is the one who drew the "backlog hygiene" line in the first place.

IDEAS, unranked:
(a) Give `what_next` a term for measured evidence: a Decision or Requirement that a `defect` TemporalFact is ABOUT scores higher, and higher again when independent instances accumulate. Small, reuses the existing vocabulary, changes a ranking nobody has to trust.
(b) Do not touch the score; add a BAND. `what_next` already separates `marked` / `ranked` / `unexplored` / `shaping` precisely because they answer different questions. A fifth band — "things the field has told you about" — reports the evidence without pretending it is commensurable with connectedness.
(c) Model the confirmation case only, which is the narrow half Anthony actually pointed at: when external evidence lands on something ALREADY ACCEPTED AND UNBUILT, say so. That is a much smaller claim than ranking, and it is the one his example supports.
(d) Nothing. Act on the reports. This is his 2026-07-30 answer and it has not been shown to have failed — the spawn defect was not unranked because ranking was missing, it was unbuilt because nobody picked it up.

⚠️ THE TRAP, AND THE GRAPH ALREADY NAMED IT. `fact:the-stale-server-defect-recurred-to-the-people-who-wrote-it-down` carries its own caveat: "recurrence is not automatically corroboration — these three share a CAUSE rather than a METHOD, so they add weight to the COST, not to the diagnosis." A naive instance count would have read three findings-by-the-same-route as three independent confirmations. Whatever counts here must distinguish *found the same way twice* from *found two different ways*, or it manufactures confidence — the same failure as `dec:` on BM25 scores not being relevances.

SECOND TRAP: a count of reports is gameable by whoever writes the most reports, and reflow2's field evidence currently comes from a small number of closely-related sources. Weighting by SOURCE INDEPENDENCE is the honest version and is much harder than counting.

NOTE ON WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this is not built twice: `report-friction` writes the reports, `TemporalFact` holds them with `basis`/`confidence`, and the reconcile family (`reconcile_artifacts` / `_verification` / `_deployment`) already turns observations into findings. The gap is not capture and not vocabulary. It is that nothing carries any of it forward into what to do next.
properties.name: OPEN — should MEASURED FIELD EVIDENCE (friction reports here, test reports in any project) be an input to what to work on next?
properties.rationale: reflow2 holds 123 measured defect facts, 70 describing recurrence, and no ranking reads any of them — while a fully-diagnosed defect with its fix already written down sat four days and recurred. The generalisation to test reports is sound. What it must answer is Anthony's own accepted decision that friction prioritisation is backlog hygiene rather than product, and the graph's own warning that recurrence by the same method is not corroboration.
